newsitem.title: USA: Mexican immigrant gets new trial in cop killing.
newsitem.headline: Mexican immigrant gets new trial in cop killing.

text.p: A Texas judge on Friday granted a new trial to a Mexican immigrant on Death Row for nearly 14 years for allegedly killing a Houston police officer.

State District Judge Werner Voigt set a Dec. 2 trial date for Ricardo Aldape Guerra, whose original conviction was thrown out by a federal judge in 1994. "It is not my intention to drag this out any longer than necessary," Voight said.

Aldape was convicted of capital murder and sentenced to death in October 1982 for the murder of police officer James Harris. The Mexican government has lobbied on behalf of Aldape, whose story has been chronicled in books, songs and movies in Mexico.

Harris was shot three times in the head when he stopped for speeding a car in which Aldape was a passenger. Aldape said from the first that Harris was shot by another man in the car, Roberto Carrasco Flores, who died in a shootout with police. The pistol used to kill Harris was found by his side.

U.S. District Judge Kenneth Hoyt threw out the conviction two years ago in a ruling that included a blistering attack on police and prosecutors, whom he accused of manipulating evidence and intimidating witnesses. Aldape was moved off Death Row in a state penitentiary after Hoyt's ruling was upheld by the U.S. Fifth Circuit Court of Appeals in August.

Defence attorney Scott Atlas had hoped before Friday's hearing that the prosecution would agree to drop the case so that Aldape could return immediately to Mexico. Aldape, now 34, is from Monterrey, Mexico, and was in the United States illegally in 1982 looking for work.
But prosecutor Casey O'Brien said the state wanted to retry the case. "The memory of Officer Harris requires it," he said.
